questions.prompt: A logic has three parts. Which part says what a formula **means**, by giving it a truth value under an interpretation?
questions.explain: Semantics is about meaning: truth values under interpretations. Syntax only says which strings of symbols are legal formulas. Calculus is the procedure that works the truth out, such as a truth table or DPLL. The trap is to pick syntax because it sounds like the language part.

questions.prompt: Fill in the missing cell of this truth-table row. Type one capital letter: T or F.
questions.code:
P Q R | P ∨ Q | Q ∧ R | (P ∨ Q) → (Q ∧ R)
F F T |   F   |   F   |        ____
questions.explain: The left side `P ∨ Q` is F, and an implication with a false left side is always T. The trap is to type F because both sides are F. An implication is false only when the left side is T and the right side is F. In the exam, type the single capital letter.

questions.prompt: Make the 4-row truth table of `(P → Q) ∨ (Q → P)`. What kind of formula is it?
questions.explain: Every row gives T, so the formula is valid. When P and Q have the same value, both implications are T. When they differ, one implication has a false left side, so that one is T. The trap is the row with P true and Q false: `P → Q` is F there, but `Q → P` is `F → T`, which is T.

questions.prompt: A knowledge base has exactly the three models shown, one per row. Which sentence is entailed by the knowledge base?
questions.code:
P Q R
T T T
T F T
F T T
questions.explain: Entailed means true in **every** model of the knowledge base. `R` is T in all three rows. `P` is F in the third model and `Q` is F in the second, and one counter-row is enough to rule a sentence out. `P ∧ Q` fails in both of those rows. The trap is to accept a sentence that is true in most models.

coldWarmup.prompt: A universe U has 20 elements. The set A holds 8 of them. How many elements are in the complement of A?
coldWarmup.explain: The complement holds everything in U that is not in A, so 20 minus 8. The trap is to add the two numbers, or to give the size of A again.

coldWarmup.prompt: In a tree, what do you call a node that has no children?
coldWarmup.explain: A leaf is a node without children. The root is the one node without a parent, at the other end of the tree. Mixing up those two is the trap.

coldWarmup.prompt: A search problem is written as a state space. What does the successor function give you?
options: The states you can reach from a state in one step
Whether a state is a goal state
The cost of a whole path
The state in which the search starts
coldWarmup.explain: The successor function lists the next states, one step away. Deciding whether a state is a goal is the job of the goal test, which is the tempting wrong answer. The starting point is the initial state.
